ai_review.summary: A superb true‑matrix capture of Boston ’73 delivers crystal‑clear sound and a smoking performance highlighted by a 19‑minute Eyes of the World and flawless transitions.
ai_review.review: The Dusborne matrix is praised as the best ever – a clean soundboard blend with audience ambience that makes every instrument shine.  The show itself ranks among the band’s finest, opening with Morning Dew, rolling through a monster second set (notably Eyes of the World, Playing In The Band and Sugar Magnolia) and featuring tight segues throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 detailed reviews consistently give 4‑5 stars, lauding both the exceptional true‑matrix recording and the high‑energy performance; weighted average of show (≈4.8) and recording (5.0) yields ~4.9.

recording_quality.technical_notes: True matrix of clean soundboard overlaid with audience; no splice artifacts, crisp mix, captures both instrument detail and crowd ambience. Reviewers call it the best matrix ever heard.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set ends strongly, second set flows seamlessly with tight transitions (e.g., Pre‑Slipknot into Sugar Magnolia). Mix of newer material and classic standards keeps energy high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is repeatedly praised as perfect and drives the epic Eyes jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal performance gets highlighted, especially his ‘Donnaskreech’ imitation during Sugar Magnolia; some reviewers note his later‑80s material felt bland.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano work is called out positively on several tracks.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s jazz‑style drumming is lauded; Mickey Hart is absent, which reviewers say avoids ‘messing up’ Bill’s feel.
